n: A psalm of trust that the apostles Peter and Paul later applied to Christ’s resurrection. David begins, “Keep me safe, O God, for I take refuge in you.”
He tells the Lord, “You are my Lord; I have nothing good apart from you.”

f.w: my goodness extendeth not to thee
f.g: Better “I have no good besides you.”

n: His delight is in the holy people of the land — God’s faithful are his true companions.

f.g: The holy ones — those set apart for God.

n: Those who chase other gods multiply their own sorrows. David will not join their offerings or even speak their gods’ names.

f.g: Pagan libations, possibly involving blood, which Israel’s law forbade.

f.w: nor take up their names into my lips

n: The Lord himself is David’s inheritance and his cup; God holds his future secure.

f.g: Like the Levites, who received no land because the Lord was their inheritance.
My allotted share, as land was distributed by lot.

n: The boundary lines of his life have fallen in pleasant places; his heritage is beautiful.

f.g: Measuring cords used to mark out land allotments.

n: David blesses the Lord, who counsels him; even at night his inner self instructs him.

f.g: Reins = kidneys, the seat of conscience and emotion — his heart teaches him at night.

n: He keeps the Lord always before him; with God at his right hand he will not be shaken.

f.w: I have set the LORD always before me

f.g: The place of a protector or defender in battle.

n: So his heart is glad and his whole being rejoices; even his body will rest secure in hope.

f.g: My soul or inner self (the Greek translation reads “my tongue,” as quoted in Acts 2:26).

f.w: my flesh also shall rest in hope

n: God will not abandon him to the grave or let his Holy One see decay. Peter taught that this was fulfilled in Jesus Christ, whose body rose before it could decay.

f.w: thou wilt not leave my soul in hell

f.g: Hebrew sheol — the world of the dead.

f.w: thine Holy One to see corruption

n: God will show him the path of life; in his presence is fulness of joy, and at his right hand are pleasures forever. A beautiful picture of eternal life.

f.w: in thy presence is fulness of joy
